name: Zobo (Hibiscus Drink)
summary: A ruby-red chilled drink of dried hibiscus petals simmered with ginger, cloves and pineapple, sweet-tart and refreshing.
story: Zobo is made from dried roselle (hibiscus) calyces and is a popular cold drink across Nigeria, especially in the north. It is served at parties, weddings and naming ceremonies, and sold in bottles on roadsides.

steps.title: Rinse the petals
steps.text: Wash the dried hibiscus in a bowl of cold water two or three times, rubbing gently, until any dust and grit settles and the water runs clear-ish red.

steps.title: Add the spices
steps.text: Put the petals in a large pot with the ginger, cloves and pineapple. Pour in the water and bring to a boil over high heat.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Reduce to medium-low and simmer for 20 minutes. The liquid should turn deep ruby and smell tangy and spicy. Longer boiling makes it bitter.

steps.title: Steep
steps.text: Turn off the heat, cover and leave to steep for at least 30 minutes. This deepens colour and flavour.

steps.title: Strain and sweeten
steps.text: Pour through a fine sieve into a jug, pressing the petals to extract all the liquid. While still warm, stir in sugar or honey until dissolved. Add a little at a time and taste, because the sourness is strong.

steps.title: Chill and serve
steps.text: Add mint if using and refrigerate for at least 2 hours. Serve over ice with citrus slices.

tips: Do not over-boil; 20 minutes is enough or the drink turns harsh.
Fresh ginger gives the signature kick; add more for a sharper drink.
Keeps for about 5 days in the fridge in a clean bottle.
Dilute with a little cold water if it is too tart rather than adding lots of sugar.

swaps.swap: Use dried hibiscus flowers sold as 'flor de Jamaica' in Latin shops or hibiscus tea; the flavour is the same.
Use a splash of pineapple juice or a few slices of apple; the drink will be slightly less fruity.
